overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by giving an ambiguous reply to an executive session minutes request and not reviewing the minutes at its next meeting. A further allegation raised late was not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to respond within 10 days to a request for executive session minutes from two 2025 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: simply suggesting that the request had been received and did not inform the complainant that it would conduct a review of the executive session minutes

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to review the requested executive session minutes at its next meeting after the request.
allegations.key_passage: Rather, the Board reviewed the executive session minutes at its meeting on May 7, 2026, which was the sixth meeting after receiving the request.

allegations.summary: In the request for further review, complainant alleged the Board did not send the AG a copy of the complaint and its response; this was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We generally decline to review an allegation that was not included within the original complaint filed with the public body because the public body has not had an opportunity to respond to the allegation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Law and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
